original_question: Do there exist, in ZFC, topological groups G and H such that each satisfies Sfin(Onbd,O) but the product G x H fails Sfin(Onbd,O)?
target_in_paper: Section 10, Problem 10.1 (Tkačenko): "Are there, in ZFC, groups G, H satisfying Sfin(Onbd, O) such that G × H does not satisfy Sfin(Onbd, O)?" ([nzdr.ru](https://www.nzdr.ru/data/media/biblio/kolxoz/M/MD/MDgt/Pearl%20E.%20%28ed.%29%20Open%20Problems%20in%20Topology%20II%20%28Elsevier%2C%202007%29%28ISBN%200444522085%29%28723s%29_MDgt_.pdf))
correct_elements: Already correct are the ZFC setting, the existential two-group form, the requirement that each factor satisfy Sfin(Onbd,O), and the failure of the same property for the product. That is exactly the content of Problem 10.1, and reading G and H as topological groups is faithful to the Section 10 context. ([nzdr.ru](https://www.nzdr.ru/data/media/biblio/kolxoz/M/MD/MDgt/Pearl%20E.%20%28ed.%29%20Open%20Problems%20in%20Topology%20II%20%28Elsevier%2C%202007%29%28ISBN%200444522085%29%28723s%29_MDgt_.pdf))
missing_details: The notation Sfin(A,B) is not defined in the draft. In the paper, Sfin(A,B) means: for every sequence (Un) of members of A, there exist finite subfamilies Fn ⊆ Un such that ⋃n Fn is a member of B. ([nzdr.ru](https://www.nzdr.ru/data/media/biblio/kolxoz/M/MD/MDgt/Pearl%20E.%20%28ed.%29%20Open%20Problems%20in%20Topology%20II%20%28Elsevier%2C%202007%29%28ISBN%200444522085%29%28723s%29_MDgt_.pdf))

The symbol O should be made explicit: it denotes the family of all open covers; and the chapter's standing convention is that covers are nontrivial, i.e. the whole space itself is not a member of the cover. ([nzdr.ru](https://www.nzdr.ru/data/media/biblio/kolxoz/M/MD/MDgt/Pearl%20E.%20%28ed.%29%20Open%20Problems%20in%20Topology%20II%20%28Elsevier%2C%202007%29%28ISBN%200444522085%29%28723s%29_MDgt_.pdf))

The symbol Onbd must be defined groupwise: for a topological group K, Onbd(K) consists of covers of the form {k·U : k ∈ K}, where U is a neighborhood of the identity element of K. ([nzdr.ru](https://www.nzdr.ru/data/media/biblio/kolxoz/M/MD/MDgt/Pearl%20E.%20%28ed.%29%20Open%20Problems%20in%20Topology%20II%20%28Elsevier%2C%202007%29%28ISBN%200444522085%29%28723s%29_MDgt_.pdf))

Because Onbd depends on the ambient group, the notation has to be interpreted separately for G, for H, and for G × H. This dependence is implicit in the paper but not visible in the draft. ([nzdr.ru](https://www.nzdr.ru/data/media/biblio/kolxoz/M/MD/MDgt/Pearl%20E.%20%28ed.%29%20Open%20Problems%20in%20Topology%20II%20%28Elsevier%2C%202007%29%28ISBN%200444522085%29%28723s%29_MDgt_.pdf))

The product should be stated as the cartesian/product topological group G × H with the product topology; the surrounding sentence in the paper phrases the issue as preservation under cartesian products. ([nzdr.ru](https://www.nzdr.ru/data/media/biblio/kolxoz/M/MD/MDgt/Pearl%20E.%20%28ed.%29%20Open%20Problems%20in%20Topology%20II%20%28Elsevier%2C%202007%29%28ISBN%200444522085%29%28723s%29_MDgt_.pdf))

Problem 10.1 itself imposes no extra assumptions such as separability, metrizability, analyticity, abelianness, or being a subgroup of Z^N. Adding any of these would alter the paper's actual scope. ([nzdr.ru](https://www.nzdr.ru/data/media/biblio/kolxoz/M/MD/MDgt/Pearl%20E.%20%28ed.%29%20Open%20Problems%20in%20Topology%20II%20%28Elsevier%2C%202007%29%28ISBN%200444522085%29%28723s%29_MDgt_.pdf))
refined_question: For a topological group K with identity e_K, let Onbd(K) be the family of nontrivial open covers of K of the form {k·U : k ∈ K}, where U is a neighborhood of e_K, and let O(K) be the family of all nontrivial open covers of K. Is there, in ZFC, a pair of topological groups G and H such that for each K in {G,H} and every sequence (Cn) of members of Onbd(K), there exist finite subfamilies Fn ⊆ Cn with ⋃n Fn ∈ O(K), while the product group G × H, with the product topology, fails this same property Sfin(Onbd(G × H), O(G × H))? ([nzdr.ru](https://www.nzdr.ru/data/media/biblio/kolxoz/M/MD/MDgt/Pearl%20E.%20%28ed.%29%20Open%20Problems%20in%20Topology%20II%20%28Elsevier%2C%202007%29%28ISBN%200444522085%29%28723s%29_MDgt_.pdf))
justification: The draft is aimed directly at Section 10, Problem 10.1, not at the neighboring Problems 10.2 or 10.3. Section 1 supplies the general meanings of Sfin(A,B) and O, while Section 10 specializes these notions to topological groups by defining Onbd and then asks exactly whether a ZFC counterexample to product preservation exists. The sentence immediately after Problem 10.1 only relates the diagonal case G = H to Problem 10.2 via finite powers, so the sharp paper-faithful refinement is the two-factor product question itself, with the notation made explicit and no extra hypotheses added. ([nzdr.ru](https://www.nzdr.ru/data/media/biblio/kolxoz/M/MD/MDgt/Pearl%20E.%20%28ed.%29%20Open%20Problems%20in%20Topology%20II%20%28Elsevier%2C%202007%29%28ISBN%200444522085%29%28723s%29_MDgt_.pdf))
